mechanism_narrative: Sustained grocery-pharmacy mobility above baseline (+2.9% at t-0w) indicates stable essential-goods demand and consumer confidence. This baseline confidence propagates to discretionary retail-recreation visits over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM positive and stable across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above +2.0% in the first two weeks of the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has declined from +7.3% to +5.3% over four weeks, signaling reduced home-confinement behavior. This deconfinement trend accelerates retail-recreation mobility as consumers exit residential spaces and increase discretionary visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.4 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility rebounds to +6.0% or higher in the first two weeks of the forecast period, and RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the baseline period mean.

This persistent suppression of transit use indicates sustained constraints on commuting and public mobility, which directly suppresses retail-recreation visits dependent on transit access over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remains between -39.9% and -45.6% across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises above -35% in the first two weeks of the forecast period and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points relative to the baseline period mean.

When combined with stable grocery-pharmacy mobility (+2.9%), this signals regime shift toward reopening. The interaction of workplace recovery and consumer confidence drives retail-recreation upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -15.0% AND GROCERY_PHARM remains above +2.0%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 18.7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES falls below -20.0% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days is lower than the last 28 days despite both proxies meeting trigger conditions.

This suppression of outdoor alternatives redirects leisure demand toward indoor retail-recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined 4.7 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -20.0% within the first two weeks of the forecast period and RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the baseline period mean.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility recovery (from -32.3% to -13.6%) combined with declining residential confinement (+7.3% to +5.3%) indicates a bifurcated reopening: workers returning to offices, residents spending less time at home. This dual shift in activity patterns generates weekday retail-recreation demand as commuters and mobile populations increase discretionary visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by >5 percentage points week-on-week AND RESIDENTIAL declines by >0.5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or RESIDENTIAL reverses trend in the first two weeks of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed the last 28 days mean by at least 2 percentage points.

candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -35.0% in week t+1w
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -40.1% and RETAIL_REC at -13.7% at t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -30.0% in the first week of the forecast period and RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points relative to the baseline period mean.

RETAIL_REC will remain below baseline over the next four weeks.
